observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: ECX is copied to EDI at 0x00c0c084 and is the receiver. Both exits end in RET 0x4 (0x00c0c0be and 0x00c0c0c7), so the callee pops the single 4-byte argument; every inspected caller therefore pushes exactly one word. The argument is read at 0x00c0c098: MOV EBP,dword ptr [ESP + 0x14], and with four entry pushes ESP is ESP0-16, so ESP0-16+0x14 = ESP0+0x04, the first pushed word.

layout.frame: four register saves (PUSH EBX, EBP, ESI, EDI), no EBP frame, no SUB ESP. 0x00c0c09c: LEA ESP,[ESP] is a zero-offset no-op emitted by the compiler as a placeholder; the loop needs no outgoing-argument area beyond the single PUSH ESI at 0x00c0c0a8.
layout.reads: ECX (the receiver), then [EDI] (the receiver vtable), then [vtable + 0xb0] and [vtable + 0xb4], then the argument word at ESP0+0x04, then the dword at element + 0x8 for each element. No global and no other field is touched.

observed_mechanics: 0x00c0c080..0x00c0c083: four PUSHes, so ESP is ESP0-16 for the whole body
0x00c0c084: MOV EDI,ECX captures the receiver in a callee-saved register, because both virtual calls clobber ECX
0x00c0c086: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDI] loads the receiver's vtable pointer, so the receiver is polymorphic
0x00c0c088: MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0xb0] and 0x00c0c08e: CALL EDX, with no PUSH between them, so virtual slot +0xb0 is a no-argument count getter
0x00c0c090: MOV EBX,EAX holds the count across the loop

0x00c0c094/0x00c0c096: TEST EBX,EBX / JBE 0x00c0c0b7 -- the guard is unsigned-below-or-equal, so a count of zero AND a count whose sign bit is set both skip the loop; the negative case is handled by the same branch, not by a separate test
0x00c0c098: MOV EBP,dword ptr [ESP + 0x14] is the only read of the argument and it is hoisted out of the loop, so the search key is loop-invariant
0x00c0c09c: LEA ESP,[ESP] computes ESP + 0 and writes nothing, so it has no effect; it is recorded because it is a real instruction in the body

0x00c0c0a0/0x00c0c0a2: the vtable is reloaded and slot +0xb4 re-read on every iteration, so a receiver whose vtable changed mid-loop would be followed, but no such mutation is possible from inside this body
0x00c0c0a8/0x00c0c0a9/0x00c0c0ab: PUSH ESI ; MOV ECX,EDI ; CALL EDX, so slot +0xb4 is a thiscall taking the loop index as its single stack argument and returning a pointer in EAX

0x00c0c0ad: CMP dword ptr [EAX + 0x8],EBP is the whole predicate: the element's dword at +0x8 against the argument, compared as a full 32-bit signed-or-unsigned equality that does not depend on the sign
0x00c0c0b0: JZ 0x00c0c0c1 takes the first match, so the search is a forward linear scan that stops at the lowest matching index
0x00c0c0b2/0x00c0c0b3/0x00c0c0b5: INC ESI ; CMP ESI,EBX ; JC 0x00c0c0a0 is a signed back edge, so the loop terminates on the first index that reaches the count

0x00c0c0b7..0x00c0c0be: the miss epilogue pops EDI, ESI, EBP, then OR EAX,0xffffffff, then pops EBX and returns with RET 0x4; the OR guarantees a full-width -1 regardless of what the count getter left in EAX

0x00c0c0c1..0x00c0c0c7: the hit epilogue pops EDI, then MOV EAX,ESI, then pops ESI, EBP, EBX and returns with RET 0x4; both epilogues pop the same four registers, so the frame is balanced on both paths
0x00c0c0c8..0x00c0c0cf: eight INT3 bytes, the standard inter-function pad

control_flow.branch_polarity: 0x00c0c094/0x00c0c096 is TEST/JBE, so the loop is skipped for count <= 0 unsigned, which also covers a negative signed count. 0x00c0c0ad/0x00c0c0b0 is CMP/JZ on equality of the full dword, so the match is exact and sign-agnostic. 0x00c0c0b3/0x00c0c0b5 is CMP/JC, a signed less-than, so the loop bound is treated as signed even though the guard above treated it as unsigned-or-equal; a count above 0x7fffffff would therefore pass the guard and then exit the loop immediately.

semantic_contract: 0x00c0c080 is a pure, non-mutating linear search over a polymorphic collection. It asks the receiver for its element count through vtable slot +0xb0, which takes no argument, and if that count is not positive it returns the sentinel 0xffffffff without touching the collection again. Otherwise it walks indices 0 upwards, asks the receiver for element i through vtable slot +0xb4, and compares element i's dword at +0x8 against the caller's key. The first match returns that index; exhausting the count returns 0xffffffff. It writes no memory, touches no global, and the receiver is only read. The sentinel is materialised by OR EAX,0xffffffff rather than MOV EAX,-1 so the miss value is a full-width -1 no matter what the count getter left behind. Its contract is pinned by three inspected callers in the same code region: 0x00c0c140 looks for id 0x0d and falls back to 0x52 only when the first lookup returns -1, 0x00c0c160 does the same for 0x27 and 0x50, and 0x00c1aed0 inlines the 0x0d / 0x52 pair. So the -1 return is a not-found marker that callers branch on, not an index. The receiver's own class is a large simulator-side object: the contiguous accessor block 0x00c0c0d0..0x00c0c1c0 reads and writes fields at +0xa60, +0xb34, +0xb74, +0xbb0, +0xbb1, +0xe80 and +0xe84 of the same object, so this search coexists with float, pointer and byte-flag state on one instance.
classification_rationale: The full 74-byte body and all 36 instructions, the ABI including the callee-cleaned argument, the argument's frame offset, both virtual slot offsets, the single element field offset, the -1 sentinel, the loop's signed back edge, the JBE guard's unsigned-or-equal polarity, the frame balance on both exits and the INT3 padding are all read directly from the disassembly, and the -1 contract is corroborated by three callers in the same code region. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for one named bound: the owning class and the concrete callees of its two virtual slots. SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, a positive-controlled .rdata/.data dword scan found no vtable entry for 0x00c0c080 or any of its eleven sibling accessors, no vtable for the receiver was located, and the offset signature matches no ModAPI declaration. The bound is therefore both the class identity and the identity of slots +0xb0 and +0xb4; the mechanics of what they do are pinned, their names are not. The search behaviour itself carries no residual uncertainty.
semantic_findings: 0x00c0c080 is a pure query: it performs no memory write, touches no global, and only reads the receiver.
The receiver is polymorphic and the search goes through two virtual slots, +0xb0 for the count and +0xb4 for element access, so subclasses can change both the collection and the element layout.
The search key lives at element offset +0x8 and the -1 return is a not-found marker, fixed by three sibling callers that branch on CMP EAX,-1.

The count guard is TEST EBX,EBX / JBE, which is unsigned-or-equal, so a negative count is skipped by the same branch; the loop's own bound test is a signed JC, so the two disagree for counts above 0x7fffffff. That inconsistency is real and is recorded rather than smoothed over.
The search key is hoisted into EBP before the loop and never reloaded, and the vtable is re-read on every iteration even though nothing in the body can change it.
LEA ESP,[ESP] at 0x00c0c09c is a genuine no-op instruction in the shipped code, left behind by a frame-size special case; it has no effect and is recorded for byte-level fidelity.

The receiver carries float state (+0xa60 dereferenced to a float at +0x574), a dword compared against 1 (+0xb34), a dword at +0xb74, two adjacent byte flags (+0xbb0, +0xbb1) and a pointer whose bytes at +0x388 and +0x389 are tested (+0xe84), so this is a rich per-object state container rather than a thin wrapper.
Neither this function nor any of its eleven siblings appears in a vtable, so the whole accessor block is a set of free functions over a concrete class and no SDK interface name applies.
unresolved_questions: The binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so no class identity can be read from typeinfo; class claims in this record rest only on observed vtable data and SDK header text.
No original-process trace exists for any function in this batch. Every statement here is static.
What class owns 0x00c0c080? The receiver's offset signature is known (+0xa60, +0xb34, +0xb74, +0xbb0, +0xbb1, +0xe80, +0xe84) but no vtable was located and no ModAPI header matches.
What are virtual slots +0xb0 and +0xb4? Their behaviour is pinned (a no-argument count and an indexed accessor) but their SDK names, if any, are not established.

What does the element dword at +0x8 denote? Every caller passes a small constant (0x0d, 0x27, 0x50, 0x52) so it is an enumeration or tag, but the enumeration is not in any ModAPI header and the writer of the field was not located.
Why does 0x00c0c140 search for 0x0d and then 0x52 while 0x00c0c160 searches for 0x27 and then 0x50? The pairs look like primary and fallback ids, but no evidence names either member of either pair.
Is 0xffffffff ever a valid index? It would require a collection of more than 0x7ffffffe elements, so in practice the sentinel is unambiguous; the code does not rely on that.
Twenty-eight of the thirty-one observed call sites were not disassembled, so only three call sites have a verified use of the return value.
Do any of the eleven sibling accessors in 0x00c0c0d0..0x00c0c1c0 belong to a different class? They share the receiver and are contiguous in the binary, which is strong but circumstantial.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00c0c080, so the claim that subclasses never change the vtable mid-scan is static-only.
A runtime differential test must observe a concrete receiver and resolve what virtual slots +0xb0 and +0xb4 dispatch to, which is the only way to name the owning class.
The count values returned by slot +0xb0 must be captured live, because the unsigned JBE guard and the signed JC bound disagree for counts above 0x7fffffff and no live count is known.
